The Portfolio answers one question for every product you sell: after what
it cost you, what Amazon kept and what the carrier charged, **what was
left?**

It answers from your own records: the money Amazon actually paid out for
your sales, and the prices on your own supplier invoices. It never uses a
fee table, and it never guesses a cost.

## What you see

- **The totals** for the period: what your sales brought in, what Amazon
  and the carrier took, and what was left.
- **Products.** One line per product, the ones that sold first, ordered by
  what they earned. After them, what is listed and has not sold yet.
- **One product in detail.** Click a product to see every figure behind
  its line, and to correct its buy price.
- **If the catalogue grew.** What more products would earn, as opposed to
  more stock of the same ones.

## Two kinds of profit

**Before your costs.** As soon as Amazon is connected and the first fetch
has finished, Biryar shows what your sales brought in less what Amazon and
the carrier took. It needs nothing from you.

**Net profit** needs one more thing: what the units cost you. Amazon does
not know that, so Biryar will not guess it. Until every sold unit has a
buy price, net profit is left blank instead of counting the unpriced
units as free, and the page names the products that are missing one.

## Giving Biryar your buy prices

There are three ways, all on the Portfolio page.

**Upload a supplier's invoice.** Drop the PDF under **Read buy prices from
an invoice**. Biryar reads every line, spreads the delivery charge over
the units, and adds the VAT you cannot reclaim. It reads invoices from
Müller, Saturn, MediaMarkt, NICI and Qogita. Nothing is saved until you
have said which line is which of your products.

**Type the price in.** Open a product and use **Correct the buy price**.

**Import a list.** For many products at once, under **Or import a cost
book**, upload a CSV file with one row per invoice line:

```
vendor,doc_number,doc_date,name,qty,unit_price,sku,shipping,prices_include_vat,vat_rate
acme,INV-1001,2026-09-30,Widget Blue,5,8.40,MY-SKU-1,3.95,false,0.19
```

The `sku` column is your own Amazon SKU, and it is the one that matters.
Amazon's records name your SKU and nothing your supplier prints, so a cost
filed under a barcode is a correct number that no sale will ever find. The
import tells you about every row it could not read and every cost it could
not match to a SKU.

## Seeing real figures before connecting anything

You do not need to connect Amazon to find out whether this is worth your
time. In Seller Central, open **Reports, Payments, All Statements** and
download a statement as **Flat File V2**. Drop that file on the Portfolio
page.

Biryar reads it and shows the period's revenue, what Amazon kept, and,
once you have added costs, what was left. **Nothing is stored.** The file
is read, the figures are shown, and none of it is kept.

It also tells you two things worth knowing:

- **Whether the file adds up.** The statement says how much Amazon paid
  out. Biryar adds up every amount in the file and compares. If the two
  disagree it says so, and tells you not to trust the figures.
- **Which fees it did not recognise.** They are listed, and they are still
  counted in the total, never dropped.

## Why the profit can look lower than elsewhere

Because Biryar counts what Amazon really took, which on a cheap product
is far more than the percentage on the fee table.
[How the fees are measured](/methodology/fees/) shows why, with figures.
